title: probationary-fallback-coordinator-and-windowed-load-trim
author: Ava Chen
commit_summaries: introduce probationary fallback coordinator to orchestrate soft-fallback windows
add windowed load trimming policy with token-weight heuristic
hook probationary coordinator into slo enforcer and regional router
add metrics/tracing for probationary windows and decision audit events
unit tests for coordinator and integration smoke for regional failover path
description: Context: During the last two incidents we observed oscillatory behavior when nodes briefly lost capacity and the global circuit opened aggressively, which caused downstream cold-start cascades and client errors. This PR implements a probationary fallback coordinator: a lightweight controller that mediates soft fallbacks (temporarily reducing token budgets and trimming request load) in a bounded window before escalating to full circuit open. Motivation: reduce noisy, immediate circuit openings while preserving SLO protection and preventing capacity thrash. Goals: 1) Give transient hotspots a short probationary period (configurable window 10-60s) where we apply conservative load trimming and tenant-specific token budgets. 2) Emit rich audit events and metrics so SRE can validate that probationary windows reduce full-circuit opens. 3) Integrate with regional routing so fallout is limited to affected zones rather than global. Major changes: - New probationary coordinator component that subscribes to SLO violation signals and maintains ephemeral per-tenant/per-route windows. - Windowed Load Trimming policy that drops or short-circuits low-value tokens according to a token-weight heuristic (configurable thresholds). - SLO Enforcer integration: coordinator can request a soft-shed action first; only if probationary windows expire or re-trigger does the enforcer escalate to deprio/circuit. - Regional router updates to prefer local probationary decisions and to fall back to cross-region only when probationary windows are saturated. - Observability: fallback_metrics and tracing for window lifecycle, decisions, and reason codes. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-8934) - [x] unit tests for coordinator logic - [x] integration smoke test for regional failover path - [x] metrics and tracing added - [x] config knobs and sensible defaults - [x] add migration notes for configmap and defaults Testing notes: ran the full serving unit test suite; created a local canary with synthetic traffic bursts to validate that probationary windows reduce circuit opens by ~62% in our simulation. Benchmarks: median p99 latency under burst was reduced by ~120ms compared to immediate circuit approach at equivalent throughput. Files changed (high level): added coordinator and policy implementations under src/serving/fallback, small surface changes to regional_router to accept probationary hints, added tests under pkg/slo and src/serving, added a Kubernetes configmap with knobs. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: mis-tuned window might delay necessary full-circuit opens for real sustained overloads. Mitigation: windows are opt-in per-tenant and default to short durations (15s) with immediate escalation if error rates exceed a hard threshold. - Risk: added complexity to routing decision path. Mitigation: minimal on-path logic; coordinator runs as separate goroutine and communicates via existing enforcer RPC with stable protobufs. Operational playbook: on rollout, enable probationary coordinator in a small subset of regions and monitor fallback_metrics.probationary.window_succeeded and .escalated counters. If we see sustained escalations or increased errors, revert configmap to disable. Release notes: Soft probationary fallback coordinator and windowed load trimming to reduce noisy full-circuit opens during transient capacity loss. How to review: focus on coordinator correctness, the token-weight heuristic, and the SLO-enforcer integration test. Related work: builds on ENG-7612 (regional routing improvements) and complements ENG-9050 (SLO enforcement hardening).

merge_summary: Merged to main via squash after approvals from Samir, Lina, and Marta. No conflicts. Post-merge action: rolled out configmap to canary regions and created a dashboard for probationary windows. Included a follow-up ticket ENG-9102 to add a runtime flag for emergency disable.
release_notes: Add probationary fallback coordinator with windowed load trimming to reduce noisy circuit openings and improve p99 latency under transient capacity loss. Default enabled only in canary regions. Config knobs available in fallback-configmap.yaml.
notes_for_ops: Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to staging for 24h, validate metrics (fallback_metrics.probationary.window_succeeded ratio > 0.5 and circuit.opens decreased), 2) Enable in two canary regions for 48h, monitor error budget burn and escalations, 3) Gradual global rollout if stable. Emergency rollback: set fallback-configmap.disable_probationary = true and restart coordinator pods.
additional_context: This PR prioritizes soft recovery strategies that reduce global impact of transient overloaded nodes. It is intentionally conservative: opt-in per tenant and short default windows. Follow-up work will include a machine-learned token-value estimator (ENG-9102) and a canary alert to auto-disable if escalation rate increases beyond baseline.
